race_context: The 'Greene Linton Stockton School Board' seats belong to Linton-Stockton School Corporation in Linton, Greene County {nces_lssc}{idoe_dir}. It runs Linton-Stockton Elementary (pre-K to grade 5), Linton-Stockton Middle School (grades 6-8) and Linton-Stockton High School (grades 9-12) {idoe_dir}. State data count 1,361 students in 2025-26 {idoe_enr}. At the Aug. 17, 2026 board meeting, Superintendent Tim Grove reported 601 elementary, 299 middle school and 370 high school students, plus 79 pre-K students {lssc_min_0817}. Grove became superintendent July 1, 2024, succeeding Kathy Goad {sboa_lssc}.

Board: five members. At the Jan. 12, 2026 organizational meeting the board elected Byron Goodman president, Jared Albright vice president and Shannon Morrison secretary; the other members are Eric Wilson and Clint House {lssc_min_0112}. Members are paid $2,000 a year, the state maximum, according to the superintendent's recommendation the board approved that night {lssc_min_0112}.

How members are elected: the 2026 ballot has a District 1 seat, a District 2 seat and an At Large seat, each 'vote for 1' {in_list}. In 2024, William E. Wilson won District 1 and Clint R. House won District 2, both unopposed {gc_2024_results}. Together these results point to two seats each for Districts 1 and 2 plus one at-large seat, with staggered terms; this guide did not find the district's written election plan to confirm this or to say whether voters across the whole district vote for every seat.

Seats on the 2026 ballot and who holds them: three of five seats. Jared Albright (District 1) and Byron Goodman (District 2) are current members running for the seats listed for them {lssc_min_0112}{in_list}. The At Large race pits Paul Shannon Morrison against Curtis W Passen {in_list}; a board member named Shannon Morrison serves as secretary, and the names suggest he is the same person, but this guide did not find a source that confirms it {lssc_min_0112}. Wilson and House, elected in 2024, are not up this year {gc_2024_results}.

An earlier vacancy: board president Katie Elliott resigned effective after May 31, 2023 to take a district finance job, and the remaining members were to appoint a replacement to serve through December 2026, according to WTWO {wtwo_elliott}{sboa_lssc}. This guide did not find who was appointed; one of the three seats on the 2026 ballot is likely that seat.
Party labels: Albright and Passen filed as Independents; Goodman and Morrison filed as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Facilities (2024-2026): on Dec. 16, 2024 the board made a preliminary decision to borrow for a '2026-2028 Campus-Wide Facility Transformation Project,' including a one-story classroom addition and a two-court gym at the secondary schools, a new chiller at the middle school, and renovations to classrooms, the track, restrooms, gyms, weight room, concessions and locker rooms, with bonds capped at $27,290,000 {lssc_prelim_notice}. The district's project page says the plan was 'designed to be tax neutral, meaning it will not result in a tax increase for residents' {lssc_facility}. The notice projected the debt service tax rate rising from $0.7799 to as much as $0.9427 per $100 of assessed value once bonds are issued, no earlier than 2026 pay 2027 {lssc_prelim_notice}.

Lease financing (2026): on May 18, 2026 the board voted to amend its lease with the Linton-Stockton High School Building Corporation so that corporation can issue up to $27,290,000 in bonds for the project, with annual lease payments of up to $3.5 million paid from property taxes {lssc_lease_det}. The board approved and signed the fourth lease amendment on July 20, 2026 {lssc_lease_exec}.

2027 budget: the district's tax notice lists a proposed 2027 budget of $19,127,695, including $12,153,526 for the Education Fund, $3,990,354 for Operations and $2,943,815 for Debt Service {lssc_form3}. It lists a maximum Debt Service levy of $3,052,457, 37.47% above the current $2,220,412, and an estimated $855,300 in property tax cap credits {lssc_form3}. The budget hearing was set for Oct. 7, 2026 and adoption for Oct. 19, 2026 {lssc_form3}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district, and no operating or safety referendum.

Other 2026 actions: the board approved policy updates from NEOLA, its policy service, and a new support staff salary scale on June 15, 2026 {lssc_min_0615}, and a staff handbook on Aug. 17, 2026 {lssc_min_0817}. Grove reported a $24,999 Digital Learning Grant for grades K-3 in June and a 90.2% IREAD passing rate in August {lssc_min_0615}{lssc_min_0817}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the candidates' views. The board meets at 6:30 p.m. on the third Monday of each month in the high school Connection Center, with work sessions at 5:15 p.m. {lssc_min_0112}; minutes are posted on the district website {lssc_minutes_2026}.
